subject: Pilot -> Contract: Ramp, Billing Definitions & True‑Up Timing
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.io>, Jonathan Cox <jonathan.cox@paygrid.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot -> Contract: Ramp, Billing Definitions & True‑Up Timing

Sara / Jonathan —

Thanks again for a great week of trials. As discussed, I attached a concise mutual action plan (MAP) and a draft SOW that maps the pilot milestones to an initial committed ramp and pricing cadence. Quick summary of what we propose: 

- 3‑month pilot (completed) followed by a staged committed ramp: 25% commit in month 1, 50% month 2, 100% month 3 (measured as committed vCPU/GPU hours and monthly committed token throughput).
- Pricing: pilot discount applied to first 3 months after signing; standard committed pricing thereafter with volume discounts at 250M/1B/2.5B billable tokens.
- True‑up cadence: proposed quarterly true‑ups (aligns billing to actual consumption, avoids monthly jitter).
- Price protection: 12 months for identical SKUs; exceptions for major infra improvements or material model upgrades.
- Billable usage definition: prompt+completion tokens excluding cache hits and server‑side prefix caching (we call out KV cache hits explicitly).

Attachments: PayGrid_MAP_v3.xlsx, SOW-draft-v2.docx.

Can you confirm PayGrid procurement needs and whether quarterly true‑ups are workable? If procurement insists on monthly true‑ups we can discuss a smoothing mechanism. Goal is to get a PO and signatures by mid‑Nov.

Thanks —
Karthik

-- 
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com]

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonathan Cox <jonathan.cox@paygrid.io>, procurement@paygrid.io
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot -> Contract: Ramp, Billing Definitions & True‑Up Timing

Karthik —

Thanks for the MAP and SOW. High level this looks promising; procurement has a few hard asks we need to resolve before a PO: 

1) True‑up cadence: our finance team prefers monthly true‑ups for forecasting accuracy. If we do monthly, we need a pragmatic way to avoid noisy adjustments (e.g., a monthly smoothing band or lookback average).
2) Price protection: legal prefers a 6‑month price protection window tied to model/sku parity. Any longer needs justification.
3) Usage definition: we need clear language on what counts as billable. Specifically, will KV cache hits, prefix cache, and intra‑session repeated prompts be excluded? We also need a definition for embeddings vs gen tokens if both are used.
4) Missed ramp remedies: if Redwood misses committed throughput, we ask for service credits and a fixed rebate schedule.

I've attached PayGrid_Procurement_Reqs.pdf with standard clauses. Can your legal and finance team review and propose language for (1) monthly smoothing, (2) 6 vs 12 month price protection, and (3) precise billing definition?

If we can get language agreed, procurement says they can issue a draft PO by Nov 20.

Regards,
Sara Liu
Head of Platform | PayGrid
[sara.liu@paygrid.io]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: PayGrid procurement asks — need commercial/legal language

Team — forwarding PayGrid's procurement list. Key negotiation points they flagged: monthly true‑ups (with smoothing), price protection length (6 v 12 months), billable usage definition (exclude cache hits), and missed ramp credits.

My suggested starting positions:
- True‑up: accept monthly true‑ups but add a 15% smoothing band and a 3‑month rolling average to dampen volatility; any adjustment under 15% of committed volume is credited but not invoiced until the quarter close.
- Price protection: offer 9 months as a compromise (we can explain improvements are unpredictable; 9 months demonstrates commitment).
- Billable usage: explicitly exclude KV cache hits, and exclude prefix cache up to a configured TTL; bill prompt+completion tokens minus cache hits. Separate meter for embeddings with tiered unit price.
- Missed ramp: service credit of 10% of committed fees for the month per missed milestone up to two months; additional credits escalate to a one‑time 25% rebate if Redwood fails to meet 3 consecutive months.

Neha — can you draft redline language for the SOW and a short clause for the MSA that covers true‑up cadence, smoothing, and price protection? Marissa — I want commercial language to present to PayGrid that keeps economics predictable.

Thanks —
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PayGrid procurement asks — proposed redlines

Karthik / Neha —

Attached is an initial commercial redline to the SOW (SOW-draft-v2.docx). High level comments I plan to propose to PayGrid: 

- True‑up / smoothing: Monthly true‑ups accepted. Implement a 3‑month trailing average for billed usage with a +/-15% smoothing band. Any month where consumption deviates beyond 15% triggers an adjustment; adjustments are applied at the quarterly invoice close to avoid cash flow noise.

- Price protection: Offer 9 months of price protection from Effective Date for identical SKUs. Carve out protections for materially improved model families or materially lower unit costs driven by new hardware families; auto‑notification required.

- Billing definition: Define "Billable Tokens" = counted prompt + completion tokens minus Cache Hits (explicitly defined as KV cache hits and server‑side prefix cache). Add a short table that separates Embedding Units (per‑1k vectors) and Gen Tokens (per‑token rate) so pricing is unambiguous.

- Ramp & remedies: Commit ramp schedule in the MAP; missed committed throughput entitles customer to service credits equal to 10% of that month's committed fee for each missed milestone, capped at two months, with a one‑time 25% rebate if Redwood misses 3 consecutive months. Include an SLA appendix for latency and availability tied to the committed tiers.

I intentionally kept the commercial remedies capped — our goal is to be accountable while protecting unit economics. If Procurement pushes monthly true‑ups without smoothing we'll run the risk of short‑term churn in metering.

I'll attach the redline. Let's aim to present to PayGrid the week of Oct 19.

Marissa
VP, Accounts | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SOW-draft-v2.docx (redline)]

From: Jonathan Cox <jonathan.cox@paygrid.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.io>
Cc: procurement@paygrid.io
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot -> Contract: Ramp, Billing Definitions & True‑Up Timing

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the redlines and the proposed compromises. Procurement reviewed and here is PayGrid's counter summary: 

1) True‑up cadence: We can accept the 3‑month trailing average as a smoothing mechanism but insist on monthly reconciliation (finalized at month close) with any net debit/credit applied the following invoice. In short: monthly measurement, quarterly cash settlement is OK.

2) Price protection: we can accept 9 months only if Redwood agrees to a 9‑month price floor on any expanded SKUs during that period (i.e., if you introduce a cheaper SKU we won't be charged the new price for our committed SKUs until the 9 months expire). Otherwise we request 6 months.

3) Billing definition: We accept the Billable Tokens = prompt+completion minus KV cache hits. We also require that KV cache hit logic be documented (TTL, hash rules) in the SOW appendix so future disputes are avoided. 

4) Missed ramp remedies: we appreciate the capped credits. Procurement requests that missed ramp credits be applied as an invoice credit rather than an operational rebate.

If Redwood accepts these points we can route a PO for signature by Nov 20. Two small asks: include the KV cache appendix and a DocuSign link for the SOW + MSA.

Best,
Jonathan Cox
Director, Cloud Platform | PayGrid
[jonathan.cox@paygrid.io]
